findings.title: High channel load
findings.detail: CORP (00:e0:fc:10:03:01, channel 11, 2.4 GHz): 80% of airtime busy, stations: 31.
findings.recommendation: The figure comes from the AP's own QBSS Load. Check the client count, a channel/width change, moving clients to 5 GHz.

findings.title: High channel load
findings.detail: CORP (00:e0:fc:10:03:02, channel 100, 5 GHz): 80% of airtime busy, stations: 31.
findings.recommendation: The figure comes from the AP's own QBSS Load. Check the client count, a channel/width change, moving clients to 5 GHz.

findings.title: WPA1 only
findings.detail: Network "Printer-Direct" advertises only WPA1 (vendor IE), no RSN.
findings.recommendation: Enable at least WPA2 (CCMP).

findings.title: BSS without HT (802.11a/b/g only)
findings.recommendation: 54 Mbit/s at most; check that it is not a disabled radio or an old AP.

findings.title: 2.4 GHz: 40 MHz channel width
findings.recommendation: In 2.4 GHz a 40 MHz channel takes almost half the band; keep 20 MHz.

findings.title: 2.4 GHz: channel is not 1/6/11
findings.recommendation: 2.4 GHz channels overlap; outside 1/6/11 an AP interferes with two neighbors at once.

findings.title: 2.4 GHz: strong BSSs on overlapping channels
findings.recommendation: Overlap is worse than sharing a channel: devices cannot coordinate via CSMA/CA and see each other as noise.

findings.title: Many BSSs on one channel
findings.detail: 2.4 GHz, channel 1: 4 BSS heard stronger than -80 dBm (SSIDs: CORP, CORP-Guest, Printer-Direct).
findings.recommendation: They all share the airtime (CSMA/CA). Consider another channel, a narrower width or lower power.

findings.title: Many BSSs on one channel
findings.detail: 2.4 GHz, channel 6: 4 BSS heard stronger than -80 dBm (SSIDs: CORP, CORP-Guest, Neighbor-2G).
findings.recommendation: They all share the airtime (CSMA/CA). Consider another channel, a narrower width or lower power.

findings.title: 802.11k is not enabled on all BSSs
findings.detail: SSID "CORP": present on 12, missing on 2 BSSs.
findings.recommendation: Check that the AP groups/profiles are the same.

findings.title: 802.11r (FT) is not enabled on all BSSs
findings.detail: SSID "CORP": present on 12, missing on 2 BSSs.
findings.recommendation: Check that the AP groups/profiles are the same.

findings.title: 802.11v is not enabled on all BSSs
findings.detail: SSID "CORP": present on 12, missing on 2 BSSs.
findings.recommendation: Check that the AP groups/profiles are the same.

findings.title: Different security across BSSs of one SSID
findings.recommendation: A client that chose one BSS may fail to connect to another. Check the SSID profile on the controller.

findings.title: Open network without encryption
findings.recommendation: For a guest network consider OWE (Enhanced Open) or a captive portal; for a corporate one, WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise.

findings.title: TKIP cipher allowed
findings.recommendation: TKIP disables 802.11n+ high rates on many clients and is deprecated; keep only CCMP/GCMP.

findings.title: WPA1 compatibility mode enabled
findings.detail: Network "IoT-Sensors" advertises both RSN and WPA1 IE (WPA2-Personal+WPA1).
findings.recommendation: Disable WPA1/TKIP unless some devices need it.

findings.recommendation: If the network should also be on 5 GHz, check the 5 GHz radio and the SSID mapping.

findings.title: 2.4 GHz: 802.11b rates in the basic rate set
findings.recommendation: While 1/2/5.5/11 Mbit/s are mandatory, management frames go out at a low rate and occupy airtime. Disable them if there are no 802.11b clients.

findings.title: Hidden SSIDs
findings.recommendation: Hiding the SSID is not protection; clients then send probes with the network name.

findings.title: HT protection enabled
findings.recommendation: The AP sees legacy clients or neighboring non-HT networks; this reduces throughput.

findings.title: 5 GHz: DFS channels in use
findings.recommendation: When radar is detected the AP must leave the channel; if users report short dropouts, compare with the radar logs on the controller.

findings.recommendation: Helps clients pick the best AP when roaming; enable it if the controller supports it.
